messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: svc-inference-high-latency (severity: P1) — initial alert at 2026-06-12T01:00:34Z

olivia (oncall): saw the page, digging in now. TL;DR: spikes in tail latency, CPU/GPU kernels show KV-cache churn.

matt (eng-runtime): adding context — we pushed a continuous-batching tweak last night that changed cold-prefix caching behavior (smaller > aggressive merge). Could be related.

diego (eng-sre): I'm pulling scheduler metrics. Noticing long queues on batch-scheduler for a subset of nodes, high backlog where short requests are stuck behind long-gen jobs.

jessica (eng-ml): curious if model quantization fallback was triggered — could increase per-token time and blow up KV entries.

olivia (oncall): customer impact: several enterprise customers reported 5-15s tail latency for embeddings and chat endpoints, errors minimal but timeouts increasing. CS loop opened. @cs-rep can you confirm top customer list?

cs-rep: Affected: acme-corp and finlytics-prod. Both saw elevated 95/99 latencies and a few client retries. They're on dedicated pools in us-west-2.

matt (eng-runtime): quick telemetry snippet:
```
batch_scheduler.queue_length{node=pool-usw2-10} ~ 120
batch_scheduler.avg_wait_ms{class=short} ~ 4500
kv_cache.evictions_per_min ~ 1800
continuous_batching.merge_rate ~ 3x baseline
```

matt (eng-runtime): logs show repeated KV cache growth and paging to SSD on nodes serving mixed workloads. Paging thrash -> stall on kernel selection -> batching fairness collapse.

olivia (oncall): ok immediate mitigations we can try (low risk):
- reduce max batch size for mixed-class route to 8
- enable preemption for short requests (experimental flag)
- temporarily pin embeddings route to quantized variant (lower memory churn)

matt (eng-runtime): running config change:
```
# hotfix: reduce batch size for mixed route
route.config.set("/v1/embeddings/mixed", {"max_batch": 8, "enable_preemption": true})
```

incident-bot: deploy started by matt at 2026-06-12T01:06:12Z — canary 10% -> 100% within 5m.

diego (eng-sre): note: preemption has some edgecases; if a short request preempts a long one, we need to ensure kernel state consistency. I'll watch KV cache metrics.

matt (eng-runtime): also toggled kv-cache.hysteresis to 0.6 (was 0.3) to avoid immediate eviction churn. Command: `kv-cache.set_hysteresis(0.6)`

jessica (eng-ml): good, that should reduce eviction storms. Also recommend bumping kv-cache.max_entries on those nodes by +20% temporarily.

olivia (oncall): I've notified the customers we have mitigations in progress. Keeping them on the hook for updates every 15m.

~12m later~

matt (eng-runtime): canary looks ok — short-request wait down from ~4.5s to 0.9s, overall tail latency improving. KV evictions still elevated but trending down.

diego (eng-sre): we saw one rollback candidate: a node hit SSD paging after the hotfix; I cordoned it and offloaded traffic. Will run a rolling drain on pool-usw2-10.

cs-rep: customers acknowledged the improvement but want RCA and ETA for full resolution.

jessica (eng-ml): follow-up: root cause hypothesis — the continuous-batching tweak increased speculative merge across prefixes, which increased KV cache footprint and forced more aggressive eviction when mixed short/long patterns arrived. That plus scheduler not prioritizing short jobs led to starvation.

matt (eng-runtime): agree. Two contributing bugs: 1) merge rate heuristics overly eager for short-window workloads; 2) scheduler fairness policy didn't implement size-based preemption correctly after the runtime change.

olivia (oncall): actions and owners:
- matt: revert/soften merge heuristics and add safety cap (deploy in next 2h)
- diego: implement a short-term scheduler rule to prioritize <200ms requests (hotfix patch) and run fleet-wide roll in 1h
- jessica: run offline eval on continuous-batching config vs mixed trace and propose permanent thresholds
- olivia: keep customers updated; coordinate post-incident RCA doc

matt (eng-runtime): quick patch we can push now (non-invasive):
```
continuous_batching.set("merge_aggressiveness", "conservative")
continuous_batching.set("max_merge_per_prefix", "2")
```

incident-bot: matt scheduled rollout at 2026-06-12T02:00:00Z — will auto-rollback on >3% error or >2x tail latency.

~30m later~

diego (eng-sre): fleet scheduler hotfix deployed to canary nodes: fairness metric is now weight-based by request-size and age. Observed median wait for short jobs drop ~85%.

matt (eng-runtime): merge cap rollback applied — KV evictions down to baseline, page faults dropping. Latency for affected customers within SLO.

cs-rep: Customers report restored performance. Acme requested a postmortem and timeline.

olivia (oncall): incident severity downgrade: P2. Summarizing post-incident notes for RCA. Preliminary timeline and mitigations will go to #postmortems.

jessica (eng-ml): root cause summary to include: continuous-batching heuristic change + insufficient scheduler preemption/fairness for mixed long/short workloads -> KV cache growth and paging -> tail latency spikes. Recommend adding regression tests with mixed traces and a canary that simulates mixed request patterns before batching changes.

matt (eng-runtime): long-term fixes: safer merge algorithm, scheduler-level size-aware preemption, add KV cache adaptive sizing based on active prefix cardinality.

olivia (oncall): final note: no data loss, customers recovered, keeping postmortem date for tomorrow 10:00am PT. Thanks everyone for the quick triage. :team-heart:
